questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That the courses was taught in English

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy enough, if I needed some information, I could just message the international office at UCC and they were good at helping.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The international office at UCC were really helpful and they replied quickly. There was orientation the first few days I arrived, and that was also helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It is hard, so it is a good idea to find something once you get accepted at the university. It is also very expensive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is nice if you choose to live in the city centre because campus is 20 minutes away from the city centre.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is very hard to find accommodation when you are a single semester student, and there is not many options.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I did find it very easy because the host institution e-mailed you with the information needed, and informed you when you needed to do something in the process.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They have an international office, and they are very sweet and helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful, I got all the classes that I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Check your e-mails, do what they tell you to do and then you will be fine.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The professors/teachers are very sweet and helpful. It is very informal unlike the professors in Denmark.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level is almost the same as it is in Denmark

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Some of my classes was just small classes were we sat around a table and listened to the teacher making a powerpoint presentation, and sometimes we would have a discussion going. Some of my other classes would just be normal seminar classes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Mental Health Law
Mental Capacity Law
Social Work and the Law (Child Law)
Juvenile Justice 
Consumer Rights: Law and Policy

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Do not choose Social Work and the Law (Child Law) because it is a master course for social workers, and the level was not very high and the teacher was very bad. Everyone was social workers students, and I was the only law student. I did not receive any information when the classes were cancelled and the social workers follow the same courses, so they know each other and get the same information. However, I will recommend the other 4 courses.

questions.answer: I did spend a lot of money during things in the weekends, and I will recommend to explore as much of Ireland as possible.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is cheaper than it is in Denmark

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There is a lot of clubs and sports available.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Almost all kinds

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Soccer because there was a lot of exchange students there as well.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Watch Gaelic football, and just see how much you can and afford while you are there!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Choose a club or society to join.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: No one

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The nature

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Find accommodation early, join a society or sports club and start on your assignments as early as possible.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Improving my English skills

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Figuring out what to read for the seminars

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Cork is a nice city!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
